p0.original: 关键问题：基因和行为如何关联
p0.en: Key issues: How genes and behaviours relate

p2.original: 塑造心理过程的根本是进化，因为它选择了那些产生适应行为的遗传变异。
p2.en: Fundamental to shaping the psychological process is evolution, as it selects genetic variations that generate adaptive behaviour.

p3.original: 正如鱼天生能游泳，大多数鸟生来就会飞，我们人类也有天生的能力。在出生时，人类的脑就已经为语言、社会交往、自我保护和许多其他功能编好了“程序”。我们可以从婴儿和他们的照料者之间的互动中观察到这些功能。例如，婴儿“知道”如何找到乳房，如何用咕咕声和哭声来进行有效沟通，以及令人惊讶的是婴儿也“知道”如何模仿他人吐舌头。
p3.en: Just as fish are born to swim, most birds are born to fly, and we humans have natural abilities. At birth, the human brain has already made “procedures” for language, social interaction, self-protection and many other functions. These functions can be observed from the interaction between the baby and their caregiver. For example, babies “know” how to find breasts, how to communicate effectively with grunts and cries, and it is surprising that babies also “know” how to imitate others in their tongues.

p4.original: 这些潜能如何成为脑结构的一部分？
p4.en: How do these potentials become part of the brain structure?

p5.original: 答案就在进化（evolution）的概念里。进化是生物体的后代为适应不断变化的环境而发生变化的过程。我们甚至可以在微观层面上观察到进化的发生过程，当细菌不断进化，进化出耐药性时，抗生素就对它无效了。当涉及更大、更复杂的有机体时，有机体为了适应气候、捕食者、疾病以及食物供应等的变化所发生的改变常常需要更长的时间跨度。例如，我们这个物种所发生的变化之一是产生了一种擅长语言表达、解决复杂问题和进行社交互动的脑。
p5.en: The answer is in the concept of evolution. Evolution is the process by which future generations of organisms change in order to adapt to changing circumstances. We can even observe evolution at the micro level, and antibiotics are not effective when bacteria evolve and develop resistance. When larger and more complex organisms are involved, changes in organisms that are adapted to changes in climate, predators, diseases and food supplies often take longer. For example, one of the changes that has taken place in our species is the creation of a brain that is good at linguistic expression, solving complex problems and social interaction.

p6.original: 进化成为遗传和行为之间的纽带。
p6.en: Evolution becomes the link between genetic and behavioural.

p7.original: 塑造心理过程的根本是进化，因为它选择了那些产生适应行为的遗传变异。
p7.en: Fundamental to shaping the psychological process is evolution, as it selects genetic variations that generate adaptive behaviour.

p8.original: 在本小节中，我们对进化的解释始于查尔斯·达尔文（Charles Darwin）的故事，他是将进化这个概念带到这个世界的人。接下来，我们将以达尔文的视角来解释遗传学（genetics），这会涉及进化的分子机制。最后，我们将探讨一门非常有趣的新学科，表观遗传学（epigenetics），它解释了我们的环境会如何影响我们的遗传框架，从而塑造了我们在各个不同领域的表现：从智力到健康和疾病，以及最终影响我们的寿命。
p8.en: In this subsection, our interpretation of evolution begins with the story of Charles Darwin, who brought the concept of evolution to the world. Next, we will interpret genetics from Darwin's perspective, which involves evolutionary molecular mechanisms. Finally, we will explore a very interesting new discipline, the epigenetics, which explains how our environment affects our genetic framework, thus shaping our performance in various fields: from intelligence to health and disease, and ultimately, our longevity.

p10.original: 2.1 描述达尔文关于进化和自然选择的理论。
p10.en: 2.1 Describe Darwin's theory of evolution and natural selection.

p11.original: 2.2 说明基因型和表现型在使每个人成为独特个体中的作用。
p11.en: 2.2 Description of the role of gene and expression patterns in making each individual a unique individual.

p12.original: 2.3 掌握表观遗传学对环境力量如何改变基因表达的解释。
p12.en: 2.3 An understanding of how the genetic force of the environment changes the expression of genes.

p15.original: 描述达尔文关于进化和自然选择的理论。
p15.en: It is a story of Darwin's theory of evolution and natural choice.

p16.original: 虽然达尔文接受的职业训练是医生和牧师，但是他最爱大自然。1831年，达尔文在他的植物学教授的帮助之下，达尔文获得了在小猎犬号（Beagle）上做“私人陪伴”的工作（Phelan，2009）。小猎犬号是一艘在南美洲进行海岸线勘探的英国科考船，这次工作机会自然令达尔文非常高兴。然而，达尔文上船后不久就晕船了，这令他很难忍受在船上的生活，因此他尽可能地待在陆地上。他满怀热情地开始研究当地的物种，收集了大量的标本并详细记录他找到的各种罕见的生物形式。达尔文非常惊讶地发现不同的动物和植物之间有很多相似性，他想知道这些动植物之间是否存在联系，并进一步地猜测，是否所有的物种（包括人类）有可能共有同一个祖先。
p16.en: Although Darwin received vocational training as a doctor and a priest, he loved nature the most. In 1831, Darwin, assisted by his Professor of Botany, was given the job of “private escort” on the Beagle (Phelan, 2009). The work of the Little Hound, a British scientific vessel that is conducting offshore exploration in South America, is naturally a great pleasure for Darwin. However, Darwin was seasick shortly after he boarded the boat, which made it difficult for him to live on the boat and he therefore remained on the land as far as possible. He has enthusiastically begun researching local species, collecting large quantities of specimens and documenting in detail the rare forms of life he has found. Darwin had been surprised to discover many similarities between different animals and plants, and he wondered whether there was a link between those animals and plants and further speculated whether all species, including humans, might share the same ancestral identity.

p17.original: 他知道这个想法与学术界公认的观点以及神创论的宗教教义背道而驰。因此，在他的名著《物种起源》（On the Origin of Species）中，达尔文仔细论证了生命的进化。这一观点饱受争议。然而，他的论点的基本内容经受住了猛烈的抨击，最终进化论在根本上改变了人们对自己和其他生物体之间的关系的看法（Keynes，2002；Mayr，2000）。
p17.en: He knew that the idea ran counter to the accepted views of the academic community and the religious teachings of the creationism. Therefore, Darwin has carefully demonstrated the evolution of life in his famous On the Origin of Species. This view has been controversial. However, the essence of his argument has survived intense criticism, which has ultimately fundamentally changed the perception of the relationship between himself and other organisms (Keynes, 2002); Mayr, 2000.

p19.original: 哪些证据让达尔文得出了物种进化这一激进结论？在旅程中，他一次又一次地观察到生物体巧妙地适应当地环境：那些吸引昆虫的花，那些长了一个非常适合敲碎某类种子的喙的鸟。但他也观察到同一物种的不同个体间的变异——就像某些人比其他人更高、视力更好一样（Weiner，1994）。这使达尔文想到这些变异可以使个体在生存和繁衍的斗争中比其他个体更具优势。然后，他提出了一种进化机制：他称之为自然选择（natural selection）的一个“淘汰”过程。经过自然选择，那些最适应环境的个体最有可能繁衍后代，而适应能力很差的个体的后代就很少，甚至他们的血统就没有传递下去［你可能听说过这叫作适者生存（survival of the fittest），但达尔文并不喜欢这个术语］。经过自然选择，一个物种会根据它所在环境的要求逐渐发生变化（见图2-1）。
p19.en: What evidence has led Darwin to reach the radical conclusion that species evolve? During the journey, he observed again and again that organisms had adapted so well to the local environment: the flowers that attracted insects, the birds that had a very suitable beak to crush a particular seed. However, he also observed variations between individuals of the same species - as some people are higher and have better eyesight than others (Weiner, 1994). This leads Darwin to think that these variations can give individuals a greater advantage over others in their struggle for survival and reproduction. He then proposed an evolutionary mechanism: what he called a “cut-off” process of natural selection. By natural choice, those who are most attuned to the environment are most likely to reproduce their offspring, and few of those who are less adaptable are, and even their bloodlines are not passed on. [You may have heard of it as survival of the fittest, but Darwin does not like it]. After natural selection, a species changes gradually according to the requirements of its environment (see figure 2-1).

p20.original: 图2-1 加拉帕戈斯群岛（Galapagos）海龟的自然选择
p20.en: Figure 2-1 Natural selection of sea turtles in Galapagos

p21.original: 当然，进化是一个情绪化的术语，因此很多人曲解了它的真正含义。例如，一些人相信达尔文的理论认为人类“起源于猴子”。但是不管是达尔文还是其他进化科学家都没有说过类似的话。相反，他们说猴子和人类在几百万年之前有一个共同的祖先——这两种说法差异是很大的。进化论认为，随着时间的推移，两个物种已经分化，每一个都发展出了不同的适应性特征。人类发展出了一个专门适应语言的脑（Buss et al.，1998）。
p21.en: Evolution is, of course, an emotional term, so many people have misinterpreted its true meaning. Some believe, for example, that Darwin's theory is that human beings “have their origins in monkeys”. But neither Darwin nor any other evolutionary scientist said anything like that. Instead, they say that monkeys and humans had a common ancestor millions of years ago — the two are very different. The theory of evolution suggests that over time, the two species have been divided and each has developed different adaptive characteristics. Human development has developed a language-specific brain (Buss et al., 1998).

p22.original: 我们应该很清楚，尽管在某些方面仍有争议，但是一个多世纪前几乎所有科学家都接受了进化的基本原则。话虽如此，我们也应该注意到进化论对于心理学来说还是一个时有争议的新东西。这并不意味着心理学家反对达尔文——事实上大部分心理学家并不反对。进化心理学为先天-后天的争议提供了一个非常优雅的解决方案——行为是从遗传和环境需求的交互过程中演变而来的（Yee，1995）。然而，有些人担心承认遗传在行为中的重要作用会引发一个问题，人们是否会把类似攻击性或成瘾等问题行为的责任推到遗传上去，对此进化心理学家响亮地回答：“不会！”（Hagen，2004）。因为，某个行为具有生物学基础并不意味着这个行为不能被改变。在本章的后面部分，我们将会探讨一些行之有效的改变行为的技术——不管这些行为源自哪里。
p22.en: It should be clear to us that, although there is still controversy in some areas, more than a century ago almost all scientists accepted the basic principles of evolution. That said, we should also note that evolutionism is a new and sometimes controversial thing for psychology. This does not mean that psychologists are against Darwin — in fact, most psychologists are against it. Evolutionary psychology offers a very elegant solution to the innate-generic controversy — behaviour evolves from the interaction of genetic and environmental needs (Yee, 1995). However, there are those who fear that the recognition of the important role of genetics in behaviour raises the question of whether responsibility for behaviour such as offensive or addictive behaviour can be passed on to genetics, and the evolutionary psychologist answered so loudly: “No! @Hagen, 2004. Because a biological basis for an act does not mean that the act cannot be changed. In the latter part of this chapter, we will explore some of the techniques that have worked well to change behaviour — regardless of where they originate.

p23.original: 在本章的后面部分，我们还将讨论一些特定的进化理论，它们可以解释攻击性、嫉妒、性取向、身体吸引力和配偶选择、教养方式、合作、气质、道德和性别差异（心理学中永恒的烫手山芋型主题）。现在，我们邀请你将自己从本小节学到的关于自然选择和适应的知识应用到一个情境中。
p23.en: In the latter part of this chapter, we will also discuss specific evolutionary theories that can explain offensive, jealous, sexual orientation, physical attraction and spousal choice, upbringing, cooperation, temperament, morality and gender differences (the eternal theme of tara in psychology). Now, we invite you to apply to a situation the knowledge you have learned from this subsection about natural selection and adaptation.

p24.original: 我们的基因有超过98%的部分在黑猩猩的基因中也能找到（Pennisi，2007）。这就支持了达尔文的观点：人和猿有共同的祖先。
p24.en: More than 98% of our genes can be found in chimpanzees (Pennisi, 2007). This supports Darwin's view that human beings and apes share a common ancestor.

p27.en: Select one of the following behaviours and discuss what adaptation it may have, so that people can better survive and develop in a given environment.

p33.original: 6. 性别差异（选择一个例子就好）

p38.original: 说明基因型和表现型在使每个人成为独特个体中的作用。
p38.en: Describe the role of gene and expression patterns in making each individual a unique individual.

p39.original: 从原理上讲，基因编码非常简单。就像CD中的微小凹坑可以编码图片或者音乐信息一样，你的基因也可以编码构成遗传特质的分子信息。想一下你个人独一无二的身体特征组合，例如，你的身高、五官特征和头发颜色等。所有这些都源自你父母亲的遗传编码“蓝图”，并被刻进你身体中几乎每一个细胞里。与之类似，基因也会影响心理特质，包括你的基本气质、恐惧倾向以及某些行为模式（Pinker，2002）。
p39.en: In principle, the gene code is very simple. Just like the tiny pits in the CD can encode pictures or music information, your genes can encode molecular information that makes up the genetic traits. Think of your unique body combinations, like your height, your five official features and your hair color. All of this comes from your parents' genetic code, Blueprint, and it's carved into almost every cell in your body. Similarly, genes can affect psychological characteristics, including your basic ethos, the tendency to fear and certain patterns of behaviour (Pinker, 2002).

p40.original: 然而，即使在遗传的影响下，你依然是不同于你父母的独一无二的个体。你的独特性的来源之一是你的经历：你成长的环境，包括时间和空间都与你的父母不同。你和父母之间差异的另一个来源是特质组合的随机性，包括身体的和心理的。父母双方把他们从祖先那里遗传的特质传给了你。（请注意，你不可能复制你的父亲或者母亲的全部基因，你只能从每一个人那里随机抽取一半。）这种混合遗传产生了属于你的独一无二的基因型（Genotype），它使你成为与地球上的任何一个其他人不同的个体。虽然每个人看起来都是不同的，但是人类基因材料的99.9%是相同的（Marks，2004）。
p40.en: And yet, even under the influence of genetics, you are still a unique individual unlike your parents. One of the sources of your uniqueness is your experience: you grow up in a different environment, both in time and space, than your parents. Another source of difference between you and your parents is the randomity of the characteristic combination, both physical and psychological. Both parents passed on to you the traits they inherited from their ancestors. (Please note that you can't copy all the genes of your father or mother, and you can only randomly extract half of them from everyone. This mixed genetic creation of your unique Genotype makes you an individual different from any other person on Earth. Although everyone looks different, 99.9 per cent of human genetic material is identical (Marks, 2004).

p41.original: 如果说基因型是“蓝图”，那么按这份“蓝图”输出的结果就是表现型（phenotype）。你的表现型包括了你所有可观测的身体和心理特征，例如，你的身高、头发颜色、运动天赋和个性（仅举几例）。虽然表现型是基于生物基础的，但它并不完全由遗传决定。遗传总是和环境协同工作的。例如，营养、疾病、应激和其他生活经历等因素会和我们的生物特质一起对人的身心特征产生影响。甚至在我们出生之前，环境就会对我们产生影响，例如，毒素或者病毒可能会导致出生缺陷。所有这些环境的影响让我们理解了为什么同卵双胞胎的基因型是相同的，但是表现型却是不同的。在本节的后面部分，我们将会探讨一门新兴的学科——表观遗传学，该学科揭示了基因和环境交互作用的机制。
p41.en: If the gene type is a blueprint, then the result of this blueprint output is a phenotype. Your behaviour includes all your observable physical and psychological characteristics, such as your height, hair color, motor gift and personality (showing just a few examples). Although the expression is biologically based, it is not entirely genetic. Genetics always work together with the environment. For example, factors such as nutrition, disease, stress and other life experiences, together with our biological traits, have an impact on the physical and mental characteristics of people. Even before we are born, the environment affects us, for example, where toxins or viruses can lead to birth defects. All of these environmental effects make us understand why the genetic type of twins is the same, but the expression is different. Later in this section, we will look at an emerging discipline - the visual genetics, which reveals mechanisms for interaction between genes and the environment.

p42.original: 但是，在此之前我们先详细了解一下构成我们基因基础的各个成分。
p42.en: But before we do that, let's go into the details of the components that make up our genetic base.

p44.original: 《侏罗纪公园》（Jurassic Park）和它的续集情节设计非常巧妙，它讲述了科学家利用基因序列创造出了恐龙，使得一个小岛上充满了古老的爬行动物。当然，这些故事本身是科学幻想，但是它们基于一个重要的科学事实，可以帮助我们理解我们这个物种的基因基础。这个事实就是我们体内几乎每一个细胞都携带着一整套可以构建有机体的生物指令。请花几分钟研究图2-2，它概述了这个重要的结构并详细解释了这个过程，可以帮助你理解接下来的内容。
p44.en: Jurassic Park and its successors are well designed, and they tell us that scientists have made dinosaurs from genetic sequences, making an island full of ancient reptiles. Of course, these stories themselves are a scientific illusion, but they can help us understand the genetic basis of our species, based on an important scientific fact. And that's the fact that almost every cell in our body is carrying a set of biological instructions that build organisms. Please take a few minutes to study figure 2-2, which outlines this important structure and explains the process in detail, which will help you understand what follows.

p45.original: 就像段落中的单词串一样，基因在染色体中也是以序列的形式存在的。但是染色体并不只有一串串基因。就像段落一样，染色体也有“标点符号”，它标记了每一个基因的开始和结束，以及特定基因的表达方式和激活时间的指令（Gibbs，2003）。然而，有时候这些指令是错误的或者基因本身有缺陷。由此产生的基因表达错误就会导致身体或发展的问题，例如，脑瘫、唐氏综合征或色盲。
p45.en: Like a string in a paragraph, genes also exist in a sequence in chromosomes. But chromosomes are not just a string of genes. Like paragraphs, chromosomes also have “point signs”, which mark the beginning and end of each gene, as well as the expression of a given gene and the time of activation (Gibs, 2003). However, sometimes these instructions are wrong or the genes themselves are defective. The resulting genetic misexpression can lead to physical or developmental problems, such as cerebral palsy, Down syndrome or color blindness.

p46.original: 每个基因都通过单个蛋白质来控制有机体的运作。反过来，千万个蛋白质构成了有机体的身体特征（表现型的部分形式）和调控身体内部操作的基础。不同个体的基因存在细微的差别，这就是达尔文注意到的个体差异的生物学基础。
p46.en: Each gene controls the operation of organisms through individual proteins. In turn, tens of millions of proteins form the basis of the physical characteristics of organisms (part of their manifestations) and of the internal operation of the body. There are subtle differences in the genes of different individuals, which is the biological basis for the differences in individuals that Darwin has noticed.

p47.original: 在更小的尺度上，基因是由微小的分子单元组成的。这个分子单元被称为核苷酸（nucleotides），它类似于基因“单词”中的字母。不过，遗传密码没有26个字母，只有4种核苷酸。因此，一个特定的基因需要千百个核苷酸组成特定模式来确定一个特定的蛋白质。现在你可以明白为什么人类基因组解码计划对科学家来说如此令人兴奋：它绘制了人类有机体中全部大约25000个基因的完整核苷酸模式，包括每个基因的不同变式（这可以解释我们的个体差异）！这些结果有望帮助我们更好地理解和治疗身体和心理障碍。
p47.en: On a smaller scale, genes are made up of tiny molecular units. This molecular unit, known as nucleotides, is similar to the letters in the gene word. However, the genetic code does not have 26 letters, but only four types of nucleotide. Thus, a particular gene requires a specific pattern of a specific nucleotide composition of hundreds to determine a particular protein. Now you can see why the Human Genome Decodement program is so exciting for scientists: it maps the complete nucleotide pattern of all about 25,000 genes in human organisms, including the different variants of each gene (which explains our individual differences). These results are expected to help us better understand and treat physical and psychological disorders.

p49.original: 注：DNA片段编码就是基因，你可以将之视为有机体结构手册中的“单词”。
p49.en: Note: The DNA segment code is the gene, which you can consider as a "word" in the organic structure manual.

p50.original: 在46条（23对）染色体中，有两条染色体特别值得注意：性染色体。根据形状的不同，它们被命名为X和Y，这两条染色体携带了男性和女性的表现型的遗传代码。我们都从生母那里获得一条X染色体。同时，我们从生父那里得到一条X或Y染色体。当它们配成一对的时候，两条X染色体（XX）编码了女性，XY的组合编码了男性。从这个意义上说，我们从父亲那里得到的染色体X或Y决定了我们的生物性别。
p50.en: Of the 46 (23 pairs) chromosomes, two are particularly noteworthy: sexual chromosomes. Depending on their shape, they are named X and Y, which carry the genetic code of the male and female expression. We all got an X-chromosomal from the birth mother. Meanwhile, we get an X or Y chromosome from our biological father. When they were paired, two X-chromosomals (XX) were coded for women and X-Y were coded for men. In that sense, the chromosome X or Y that we get from our father determine our biological sex.

p52.original: 我们对基因和遗传的大部分讨论同样也适用于果蝇和蝴蝶，蜀葵和人。所有生物都遵循同样的基本遗传规则。物种间的差异来自于遗传“单词”——基因本身的差异，基因是生命单词表中的4个字母（核苷酸）的不同“拼写”组合。换句话说，我们这个星球上的所有生物的遗传代码都是由这4种核苷酸组合起来的，只是组合的模式和顺序不同。
p52.en: Much of our discussion of genes and genes also applies to fruit flies and butterflies, acacias and humans. All organisms follow the same basic genetic rules. Differences between species arise from the genetic “single word” — the genetics themselves, which are a different combination of the four letters (nucleic acid) in the life-word table. In other words, the genetic code of all the organisms on our planet is a combination of these four types of nucleotide, with different patterns and sequences.

p53.original: 这一切与心理学有什么关系呢？简而言之，基因会影响我们的心理特征，就像它们会影响我们的身体特征一样。基因可以影响多种人类特性，例如，智力、个性、心理障碍、阅读障碍、语言障碍和（也许）性取向。甚至，我们的恐惧也可能有一些遗传基础（Hariri et al.，2002）。但是，因为遗传心理学仍然处于起步阶段，我们才刚刚开始了解特定基因如何以及在多大程度上参与心理过程（Rutter，2006）。虽然某些疾病（例如，囊性纤维化）可以追溯到单个基因突变，但是大多数疾病都涉及多个基因，这使得识别基因和行为之间的联系变得非常困难（National Human Genome Research Institute，2012）。
p53.en: What does it have to do with psychology? In short, genes affect our psychological characteristics, just as they affect our physical characteristics. Genetics can affect a wide range of human characteristics, such as intelligence, personality, mental impairment, reading impairment, speech impairment and (perhaps) sexual orientation. Even our fears may have some genetic basis (Hariri et al., 2002). However, as genetic psychology is still in its infancy, we have only just begun to understand how and to what extent a particular gene is involved in the psychological process (Rutter, 2006). While certain diseases (e.g., cystalfibrosis) can be traced to individual gene mutations, most diseases involve multiple genes, making it very difficult to identify the link between genes and behaviour (National Human Geneme Research Institute, 2012).

p54.original: 那么，这是否意味着遗传决定了我们的心理？你长大了之后会像你的叔叔吗？别担心。虽然你和你叔叔的一些基因是相同的，但是遗传从不会单独起作用。遗传和环境一直都是协同工作来影响我们的行为和心理过程的（Pinker，2002）。例如，吉尔·波特·泰勒的智力几乎可以肯定是有遗传基础的（她的母亲来自哈佛，她的父亲有博士学位），但是同时她的童年环境和受到的教育进一步培养了她。她克服了中风的困难，重建新生活，并当选《时代周刊》（Time）评选的“100位世界上最具影响力人物”（2008），她将这种创造力归功于她的父亲——但是她作为科学家受到的训练毫无疑问会增强她的这种能力。
p54.en: So, does that mean genetics determines our mind? Will you be like your uncle when you grow up? Don't worry. Although you and your uncle have the same genes, the genes never work alone. Genetics and the environment have always worked together to influence our behaviour and psychological processes (Pinker, 2002). For example, Jill Potter Taylor's intelligence can almost certainly be genetic (her mother from Harvard, her father has a doctorate), but at the same time her childhood environment and the education she received further nurtured her. She overcomes the difficulties of a stroke, rebuilds her new life and is elected to the Time's selection of “100 most influential people in the world” (2008), and thanks this creativity to her father — but her training as a scientist will undoubtedly enhance her ability to do so.

p55.original: 2.3 表观遗传学的美丽新世界
p55.en: 2.3 A beautiful new world of genetics

p57.original: 掌握表观遗传学对环境力量如何改变基因表达的解释。
p57.en: It is important to understand how genetics can change genetic expression by environmental forces.

p58.original: 现在，你已经了解你是你的基因和你所处的环境共同作用的独特产物。“先天或后天？”这个历史悠久的问题已经过时了，现在取而代之的是“先天和后天”这一说法。更进一步的是，21世纪的科学对此提出了新的见解，认为环境不仅塑造了我们的表现（换句话说，我们的表现型），而且很明显它也能在分子水平上影响我们。确实如此，应激和营养等环境因素可以决定我们的基因如何运作。因此，仅仅说“先天和后天”是不够的，我们必须说“先天和后天，以及后天对先天的影响”。是不是被绕糊涂了？不用担心，让我们来给你解释一下这一非常复杂却非常有趣的新学科，表观遗传学，它研究环境如何改变基因表达。
p58.en: Now, you've learned that you're a unique product of your genes and your environment. "What is it that is born or what is left of it? “This long-standing issue is outdated and is now replaced by the term “innate and acquired”. What is more, the science of the twenty-first century offers new insights into it, considering that the environment not only shapes our performance (in other words, our performance), but also clearly influences us at the molecular level. Indeed, environmental factors such as stress and nutrition can determine how our genes work. Therefore, it is not enough to say “innate and the day after”, and we must say “innate and the day after, and the influence of the day after”. Are you confused? Don't worry, let's explain to you this very complex but very interesting new subject, the epigenetic, that studies how the environment changes genetic expression.

p60.original: 首先，让我们简要回顾一下我们对基因组的了解。你的基因组是你自己的遗传编码，它来自于你亲生父母的基因的随机组合。这个基因组或“蓝图”被编进了你身体中的每一个细胞里，被写进了DNA分子中。我们每个人的基因组都有超过25000个基因，分布在每个细胞中大约30亿对DNA中。
p60.en: First, let us briefly review our understanding of the genome. Your genome is your own genetic code. It comes from the random combination of genes of your biological parents. This genome or blueprint is encoded into every cell in your body and written into DNA molecules. Each of us has over 25,000 genes, distributed in about 3 billion pairs of DNA in each cell.

p62.original: 现在，让我们在基本框架中添加几个新概念。首先，我们来看一下DNA的一个令人惊讶的特点：单个DNA分子的长度和成年人的平均身高差不多。那么，数以十亿计的DNA对是如何挤进我们身体的每一个小小细胞中的呢？答案在于DNA的双螺旋结构：DNA分子扭成一个紧密的线圈，这样1.5～1.8米的DNA链实际上就只占据很小的一个空间。（想象一下有一根很长的线，然后开始一圈一圈地转，这样它就以螺旋的方式开始从下往上盘起来了。这根线最终所占据的物理空间就远小于它拉直了的时候所占的空间。）DNA压缩和缠绕的时候，它会把自己绕在一种特殊的蛋白质上，就像线绕在线轴上一样（见图2-3）。这种蛋白质被称为组蛋白（histone）。
p62.en: Now, let us add a few new concepts to the basic framework. First of all, let's look at one of the surprising characteristics of DNA: the length of a single DNA molecule is similar to the average height of adults. So, how do billions of DNAs fit into every tiny cell in our body? The answer lies in the double-helicopter structure of DNA: DNA molecules are twisted into a tight coil, so that the 1.5-1.8 metre DNA chain actually occupies only a very small space. (Imagine a long line, and then start to circle around, so that it starts to go down and up in a spiral. This line eventually occupies a much smaller physical space than it occupied when it pulled straight. When DNA is compressed and entangled, it surrounds itself with a particular protein, just like a wire around an online axis (see figure 2-3). This protein is called histone.

p63.original: 图2-3 我们的经历和环境如何影响我们的DNA
p63.en: Figure 2-3 How our experiences and environment affect our DNA

p64.original: 注：DNA将自身缠绕在组蛋白上。随着内部或外部的信号引导某些基因关闭或打开，DNA上会留下某些化学标记，从而改变基因组的物理结构。这些化学标记造就了表观基因组。
p64.en: Note: DNA entanglements itself to a mass of proteins. As internal or external signals lead to the closing or opening of certain genes, certain chemical markers are left on DNA, thereby altering the physical structure of the genome. These chemical markers make the look genome.

p65.original: 一个有趣的事实是，如果把你所有的DNA分子首尾相连，其尺度可以从地球往返太阳两趟！
p65.en: It's an interesting fact that if you connect the tails of all your DNA molecules, the scale can travel from Earth to the Sun twice!

p66.original: 接下来，让我们问另一个问题：如果我们所有的细胞都包含相同的基因序列（它们确实是这样），那么它们是怎么发展成不同的样子的呢？例如，为什么有些细胞会变成皮肤细胞，而另一些则会变成肌肉，还有一些会变成脑中的神经元？答案既有先天的，也有后天的：来自身体内部和外部环境中的信号会在特定的细胞中“打开”某些基因，“关闭”另一些基因。例如，随着胚胎的发育，胎儿体内的信号会激活某些特定的基因并且失活另一些基因，通过这样的方式，这些信号就可以引导某些细胞变成皮肤、肌肉，等等。然后，婴儿出生之后，在整个生命周期之中，体内的生物信号会持续引导生长发育，使得婴儿变成儿童，儿童变成青少年，青少年变成成年人。除了这些内部信号之外，细胞还会接收环境中的信号，因此，生活中的各种经验也会传递给基因组，使得不同的基因激活或失活。
p66.en: Then let us ask another question: If all of our cells contain the same genetic sequence (which they do), how do they develop differently? For example, why would some cells become skin cells, others become muscles, and others become neurons in the brain? The answer is innate and acquired: signals from inside and outside the body “open” some genes in a given cell, “close” others. For example, as the embryo develops, signals in the foetus activate certain specific genes and lose other genes, in such a way that they can guide certain cells to skin, muscle, etc. After the birth of the child, the biological signals in the body continue to guide growth and development throughout the life cycle, making the baby a child, a child a child and a child an adult. In addition to these internal signals, cells receive signals from the environment, so that life experiences are passed on to the genome, which activates or loses life of different genes.

p67.original: 在我们的一生中，这些内部和外部的信号一直在控制基因的打开关闭。每出现一次这种情况就会留下一个化学标记以记录发生了什么事情，这种记录本质上相当于是对特定细胞的所有影响的一个日志。某些标记会留在DNA上，而另一些标记会留在组蛋白上。这些残留的化学标记构成了表观遗传组（epigenome）——“epi”的意思是“在表面”——因此本质上表观遗传组是在原始蓝图上的一组“注释”。虽然原始蓝图，也就是我们的DNA，在我们的一生中保持不变，但是表观遗传组是灵活的，它会适应环境的变化，根据生物体的经历来关闭或打开基因。
p67.en: In our lifetime, these internal and external signals have been controlling the opening of genes. Each time this occurs, a chemical mark is left to record what happened, which is essentially a log of all the effects on a given cell. Some marks will remain on DNA, while others will remain on group proteins. The chemical markings of these residuals constitute a set of “notes” on the original blueprint, since the expression “epi” means “on the surface”. While the original blueprint, our DNA, has remained unchanged throughout our lives, the genetic array is flexible and adapts to changes in the environment, closing down or opening genes based on the experience of organisms.

p68.original: 2.3.3 生活经历如何改变表观遗传组
p68.en: 2.3.3 How life experience changes the appearanceal genetic group

p69.original: 教养方式在儿童的发展和行为表现中扮演重要作用可能已经不足为奇了，但是近期表观遗传学的研究为这一现象提供了新的科学解释。该领域的早期研究关注大鼠对新生幼鼠的母性行为。一些母鼠会很积极地舔舐它们的幼鼠，而另一些母鼠则很少这样做（这是养育行为中的常见变异）。那些经常被母鼠梳理毛发或舔舐的幼鼠成长为轻松随和的成年鼠，而那些很少被舔舐的幼鼠则更加焦虑、容易紧张，甚至更有攻击性。对这些大鼠的表观遗传序列的进一步检查发现早期的毛发梳理和舔舐会使得某些基因有更多的表达，这些基因有助于关闭应激反应。因此，当被细心母鼠养大的大鼠遭遇正常的应激事件时，它们的身体能更有效地处理这些应激，更快地恢复正常状态，而那些由不那么细心的母鼠养大的大鼠的表现就没有那么好（Francis et al.，1999，Weaver et al.，2004）。
p69.en: While it may not be surprising that upbringing plays an important role in the development and behaviour of children, recent research in the field of superficial genetics has provided new scientific explanations for this phenomenon. Early studies in this area focused on maternal behaviour among newborn mice. Some female mice are very active in licking their juvenile mice, while others rarely do so (this is a common variation in parenting). Those who are often brushed or licked by mice grow into easy adult rats, while those who are rarely licked are more anxious, nervous and even more aggressive. Further examination of the genetic lineage of these rats revealed that early hair combing and licking could lead to more expression of certain genes that could help to turn off stressors. Thus, when rats are taken in by a careful mother, their bodies are able to deal more effectively with these stressors and to return to normality more quickly, and those rats that are raised by less careful rats are less well performing (Francis et al., 1999, Weaver et al., 2004).

p70.original: 为什么我们要研究大鼠如何应对应激？
p70.en: Why do we have to study how rats respond to stress?

p71.original: 大鼠的生理机制与人类的非常相似。不管是大鼠还是人类，应激反应持续的时间越长，心血管系统遭受的潜在损伤就越大。因此，应激和心脏疾病之间就有明确的联系。对于人类，早在20年前我们就知道抚触婴儿可以减少健康婴儿和高危婴儿的焦虑和应激激素的生成（Field，1995）。这两个例子中的表观遗传机制可能是相同的：大鼠的舔舐和梳理行为这类生理刺激可能和抚触婴儿类似，都可以促进更有效的应激反应系统的发展。
p71.en: The physical mechanisms of rats are very similar to those of humans. The longer the stress lasts, the greater the potential damage to the cardiovascular system, both in rats and in humans. Thus, there is a clear link between stress and heart disease. For humans, 20 years ago we knew that touching babies could reduce the generation of anxiety and stress hormones for healthy babies and high-risk babies (Fild, 1995). The genetic mechanisms that can be seen in both examples may be the same: physical irritation, such as licking and combing in rats, may be similar to touching infants and can contribute to the development of more effective stress systems.

p72.original: 这些发现也展示了父母对婴儿（啮齿动物或人类）的早期养育具有适应性。由细心的母亲在富足的环境（充足的食物、危险很少）中抚养长大的婴儿能够发展出适应良好的应激反应系统来应对一个安全的抚养环境：这就好像如果妈妈说环境是安全的，那么婴儿也没有什么需要焦虑不安的。其背后的实质就是——母亲的行为影响了幼崽的表观遗传组，增加了幼崽的生存机会。然而，焦虑可能有助于个体在更具威胁性的环境（例如，缺乏食物的环境）中生存，因此由粗心母亲养大的容易焦虑的大鼠可能更适应高挑战的环境。高焦虑使我们保持了对潜在危险和捕食者的警觉。
p72.en: These findings also demonstrate the adaptability of parents to early infant care (rodents or humans). A baby raised by a caring mother in a rich environment (sufficient food, few risks) can develop a well-adapted stress system to cope with a safe environment: it is as if the mother said the environment was safe, then the baby had nothing to worry about. The essence of this is that the mother's behaviour affects the pups' superficial genetic group and increases their chances of survival. However, anxiety may help individuals to survive in more threatening environments (e.g. food-deficit environments), so that rats raised by careless mothers who are vulnerable to anxiety may be more adapted to high-challenging environments. High anxiety keeps us alert to potential dangers and predators.

p73.original: 当然，焦虑并不总是一种优势，人类的养育行为也并不总是对婴儿和儿童有利的。对儿童的虐待和疏于照顾就是令人担忧的例证。对大鼠的研究是否表明虐待和忽视可能会提升儿童罹患焦虑和应激相关疾病的风险？最近对人类的研究表明：那些童年期受到虐待的自杀个体的脑部尸检报告发现他们的大脑发生了一些与长期应激相关的改变。而童年期没有受虐待的自杀个体的脑显示出正常的应激反应模式（McGowan and others，2009）。童年经历确实会造成某些表观遗传修饰，它们会影响脑的发育。
p73.en: Of course, anxiety is not always an advantage, nor are human parenting behaviour always beneficial to infants and children. Child abuse and neglect are worrying examples. Has the study of rats shown that abuse and neglect can increase the risk of anxiety and stress-related diseases among children? Recent human studies have shown that brain autopsy reports of individuals who were abused during their childhood found that their brain had undergone some changes related to long-term stress. The brain of a suicide individual who was not abused during childhood shows normal stress patterns (McGowan and others, 2009). Childhood experience does result in some formative genetic modifications that affect brain development.

p74.original: 运动、营养和毒素也能影响基因表达（打开或关闭）的过程。一项研究发现每周两小时的有氧运动持续6个月之后可以让与肥胖和二型糖尿病有关的基因不再表达（Ronn and others，2013）。定期锻炼有助于限制与慢性炎症相关的基因表达，慢性炎症与多种疾病存在联系，包括哮喘、心脏病、自身免疫性疾病、牙周疾病、慢性疼痛、关节炎、痴呆和多种癌症（Ntanasis-Stathopoulos and others，2013）。
p74.en: Sport, nutrition and toxins can also influence the process of genetic expression (opening or closing). A study found that an aerobics two hours a week lasts six months and that genes associated with obesity and type 2 diabetes can be removed from expression (Ronn and others, 2013). Regular exercise helps to limit genetic expression associated with chronic inflammation, which is linked to a variety of diseases, including asthma, heart disease, self-immunological diseases, dental choreography, chronic pain, arthritis, dementia and various cancers (Ntanasis-Stathopoulos and others, 2013).

p75.original: 饮食对表观遗传组的影响还处于起步阶段，但是科学家发现食物会影响蜜蜂幼虫的发育，蜜蜂幼虫在基因上是相同的，而食物可以决定它们发育成不育的工蜂还是具有生育能力的蜂王（Kucharski and others，2008）。要成为蜂王的幼虫被喂食了大量的蜂王浆，这有助于它们发育出成熟的卵巢，而其他幼虫则只获得了少量蜂王浆，因此成为不育的工蜂。同样，西蓝花、抱子甘蓝和大蒜中的某些食物成分可以通过改变表观遗传组来抑制癌细胞的生长（Do and others，2010）。“暴露于空气污染物中”已被证实也会影响表观遗传组，目前研究正在考察其对肺部和呼吸系统疾病、癌症到精神分裂症等疾病的影响（Silveyra and others，2012）。
p75.en: The effects of diet on the watch genetic group are still at an early stage, but scientists have found that food affects the development of bees, which are identical in genetic terms, and that food can determine whether they develop into sterile workers or productive bees (Kucharski and others, 2008). The larvae that would become bee kings were fed a great deal of beehive mammoth, which helped them to develop mature ovaries, while the other larvae received only a small amount of beehive mammoth and became infertile workers. Similarly, certain food components in Western Blue Flowers, cuddles and garlic can inhibit the growth of cancer cells by changing the appearanceal genetic group (Do and others, 2010). The “exposure to air pollutants” has also proven to affect the surface genetic group and its effects on diseases such as lung and respiratory diseases, cancer to schizophrenia are being examined (Silveyra and others, 2012).

p76.original: 总而言之，这项表观遗传研究为我们长辈长期以来的告诫“人如其食”提供了科学证据。它也揭示了很多我们已知多年的发现（例如，抚触对婴儿的影响，运动对健康和衰老的作用）其背后的机制。一些研究表明，表观遗传的变化甚至能传递给我们的后代，因此父母所接触到的环境条件（例如，饥饿、应激和毒素）会给子辈甚至孙辈的基因组留下持久的印记。这一热门领域正在不断拓展，请关注其持续发展。
p76.en: In sum, this genetic look provides scientific evidence of the long-standing warning of “humans like their food” by our elders. It also reveals the mechanisms behind many of the discoveries that we have known for many years (e.g., the impact of touching on infants, the role of sport in health and ageing). Some studies have shown that changes in the appearance of genetics can even be transmitted to our offspring, so that the environmental conditions to which parents are exposed (e.g., hunger, stress and toxins) leave a lasting mark on the genomes of younger and even grandchildren. This topical area is expanding and attention is drawn to its continued development.

p77.original: 心理学很有用 选择孩子的基因
p77.en: Psychology is useful. Choose the child's genes.

p78.original: 科学家已经有能力控制和改变动物的基因，就像已经去世的著名绵羊多莉（Dolly），它没有父亲，1996年科学家用它母亲的一个细胞克隆了它。从那之后，虽然成功率只有1%到2%，但各种不同的克隆动物仍诞生了，从猫到牛都有（American Medical Association，2010）。不过，操控人类基因的前景如何？这有可能实现吗？现存哪些挑战？
p78.en: Scientists had the capacity to control and alter the genes of animals, like the dead Dolly, who had no father and had cloned it with a cell of his mother in 1996. Since then, although success rates range from 1 to 2 per cent, a variety of cloned animals have been born, ranging from cat to cow (American Medical Association, 2010). However, what are the prospects for manipulating the human genome? Is that possible? What are the challenges?

p79.original: 随着对基因组了解的加深，研究人员开始探讨人类在能力、情绪和抗压能力存在个体差异的基因基础（Kosslyn et al.，2002）。那些影响数百万人的疾病引发的关注更多，如癌症、心脏病、孤独症和抑郁症。现在我们已经可以从胚胎细胞中进行取样并查看是否存在某种基因缺陷，例如，唐氏综合征、肌营养不良症和镰刀型细胞贫血症。虽然很多人支持基因检测，但是另一些人担心技术进步的速度过快会导致我们没有能力解决某些伦理问题。如何使用技术来进行某种基因选择？
p79.en: As knowledge of the genome deepens, researchers begin to explore the genetic base of individual differences in human abilities, emotions and resistance (Kosslyn et al., 2002). Diseases affecting millions of people, such as cancer, heart disease, autism and depression, have attracted more attention. We can now sample embryonic cells and see if there is some genetic deficiency, such as Down syndrome, muscular malnutrition and sickle-cell anaemia. While many people support genetic testing, others fear that the speed of technological progress will lead to our inability to resolve certain ethical issues. How can technology be used to make a genetic choice?

p80.original: 胚胎植入前遗传诊断（preimplantation genetic diagnosis，PGD）这种技术可以帮助夫妇降低生出患有严重基因疾病孩子的风险。通过在早期阶段进行胎儿或胚胎测试，生殖科学家可以确保胎儿的基因健康。自1990年PGD诞生以来，其应用范围不断扩大。目前，美国和其他一些国家允许使用PGD进行性别选择：有一半的PGD诊所也给父母提供了性别选择的服务（Adams，2010）。此外，“救星宝宝”的这种业务也得以开展，那些孩子生了重病（例如，白血病）的父母可以再生一个拥有合适骨髓的孩子来拯救那个患病的孩子（Marcotty，2010）。几年前，洛杉矶的一家生育诊所宣布他们计划为客户提供包括身高、发色和皮肤颜色在内的身体特征的基因选择服务（Naik，2009）。［有趣的是，这家诊所在收到梵蒂冈（Vatican，天主教教廷所在地）的反对信后取消了该服务］。
p80.en: The technique of pre-embracing genetic diagnosis (preimplantation genetic diagnosis, PGD) can help couples reduce the risk of having children with serious genetic diseases. Reproductive scientists can ensure the genetic health of the foetus by testing the foetus or embryo at an early stage. Since the inception of the PGD in 1990, its application has been expanding. Currently, the United States and some other countries allow the use of PGD for sex selection: half of the PGD clinics also provide sex selection services to parents (Adams, 2010). In addition, this kind of operation has been carried out for the “Salvaging Baby”, where parents who have had serious illnesses (e.g. leukemia) can regenerate a child with the right bone marrow to save the sick child (Marcotty, 2010). A few years ago, a fertility clinic in Los Angeles announced that they planned to provide genetic selection services to clients for physical characteristics, including height, hair colour and skin colour (Naik, 2009). [Interestingly, the clinic cancelled the service upon receiving a letter of objection from the Vatican (Vatican, where the Catholic Holy See is located).]

p81.original: 无疑，在这个新的基因世界中，许多父母希望他们的孩子长得聪明又好看——但是智力和长相的评判标准是什么？是每一个人都可以定制自己孩子的基因，还是只有富豪才可以？可以肯定的是，我们面临的问题将同时涉及生物学、心理学、政治学和伦理学（Patenaude et al.，2002）。
p81.en: Undoubtedly, in this new genetic world, many parents want their children to be smart and good-looking — but what are the criteria for judging intelligence and appearance? Is it possible for everyone to customize their children's genes, or is it only for rich people? It is certain that the problems we face will involve biology, psychology, political science and ethics at the same time (Patenaude et al., 2002).

p82.original: 心理学家已经为如何更好地应用基因知识提供了指导（Bronheim，2000），特别是帮助人们就家庭生育计划进行基因风险评估。我们请你来回答下述问题。当然，这些问题没有“正确”答案；然而，你的回答将有助于你确定自己在这些重要议题上的立场，这些议题都是你在21世纪将会面对的。
p82.en: Psychologists have provided guidance on how to better apply genetic knowledge (Bronheim, 2000), particularly in helping people to carry out genetic risk assessments on family birth programmes. We ask you to answer the following questions. Of course, there are no “right” answers to these questions; However, your answer will help you to determine your position on these important issues, which you will face in the twenty-first century.

p85.original: 如果你可以为你的孩子选择3个基因特质，你会做什么选择？如果许多人都选择了相同的特质，你觉得这会对世界产生什么样的影响？
p85.en: If you could choose three genetic qualities for your children, what would you do? If many people have chosen the same trait, what do you think would happen to the world?
